new_entities.name: Vitamin A deficiency
new_entities.description: Low vitamin A status sufficient to impair epithelial, immune, or hematologic function.

edges.effect_quant: In a 1,060-child Thai study, serum retinol was significantly associated with hematocrit, serum iron, ferritin, and transferrin saturation, linking lower vitamin A status to poorer iron handling in children.
edges.population: children with low or marginal vitamin A status
edges.mechanism: Vitamin A supports hematopoiesis, immunity, and mobilization of stored iron, so deficiency can worsen anemia even when iron intake is not the only limiting factor. In children, this often appears as poorer hemoglobin response and less efficient use of available iron stores.
edges.summary: Low vitamin A status can contribute to poorer iron status in children, although the signal is more modest and biologically intertwined than classic iron-deficiency alone. Supplementation studies and child cohorts suggest that inadequate vitamin A can worsen anemia-related outcomes, even if the effect on ferritin or iron deficiency itself is not always uniform across populations.
edges.caveats: Most stronger data come from supplementation studies rather than directly observing vitamin A deficiency as an exposure, so this edge involves some causal inference from reversal evidence. Effects depend on baseline deficiency burden, inflammation, infection exposure, and whether other micronutrient deficits are also present.

evidence.citation: Bloem MW et al 1989 Am J Clin Nutr
evidence.notes: Iron metabolism and vitamin A deficiency in children in northeast Thailand.

evidence.citation: Andersen AB et al 2016 Asia Pac J Clin Nutr
evidence.notes: The effect of daily consumption of the small fish Amblypharyngodon mola or added vitamin A on iron status: a randomised controlled trial among Bangladeshi children with marginal vitamin A status.
